title: Security incident quick reference and postmortem template
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact on-call quick reference and postmortem template for security incidents at Redwood Inference. Intended for use by on-call engineers, security responders, and incident commanders. Keep this doc open during an incident; copy sections into the incident channel and the postmortem doc afterwards.

Scope:
- Covers initial triage, containment actions that rely on RBAC v2 and audit log lookups, SIEM export checklist, evidence automation pointers, and a postmortem template with artifacts checklist.
- Not a replacement for the full IR runbook; use alongside the full playbooks in Confluence.

-----------
Quick severity guide (for on-call use):
- Sev 0 (critical): Active data exfiltration, customer PII exposure, infra compromise (ongoing). Paging: security oncall + SRE lead.
- Sev 1 (high): Compromised credentials detected, suspicious lateral movement, production API abuse. Page security oncall.
- Sev 2 (medium): Anomalous but contained activity, failed brute force, unusual API volume from single key. Notify through channel, raise incident ticket.
- Sev 3 (low): Non-urgent anomalies, scanning activity without access. Log and monitor.

Immediate triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
- Create incident in JIRA (JIRA-SEC-<timestamp>) and open #sec-incident-<id> on Slack.
- Assign roles: IC (incident commander), Lead Responder, SRE liaison, Communications.
- Capture scope: systems, services, keys involved, suspected impact. Quick bullet list.
- Preserve evidence: do NOT reboot machines. Snapshot logs, copy relevant KV caches if safe.
- Apply short-term containment if evidence of ongoing access (see containment actions).

Containment actions (high-confidence immediate steps):
- Rotate secrets/keys associated with compromised principal: use internal secrets rotation pipeline (runbook command: scripts/rotate-key --principal <id>) or via Redwood Console -> Secrets -> Rotate.
- Revoke sessions for principal via RBAC v2: run authctl revoke-sessions --principal <principal-id> --reason "incident-<id>".
- Limit role permissions temporarily: change rbac policy to read-only for affected role (example command): rbacctl patch-role --role <role-name> --policy "deny:write,exec" --apply-now.
- Isolate host(s) at network layer: update firewall rule set in VPC console: block outbound to unknown IPs. SRE to apply.
- For hosted API abuse: enable per-key rate limiting and set route fallback to safe model variant in Redwood Console (Route -> Edit -> Fallback: true).

RBAC v2 quick commands and notes:
- List roles for principal: rbacctl list-principals --principal <id> --format table
- Show effective permissions: rbacctl eval --principal <id> --resource <resource>
- Temporarily remove role binding: rbacctl unbind --principal <id> --role <role-name> --dry-run (review) then run without --dry-run.
- Important: audit log will show role changes; do not rely on console UI as sole evidence source — export server-side audit for chain-of-custody.

Audit log lookups (examples):
- KQL example for SIEM (search suspicious key usage):
  event.type: "auth" AND event.action: "token.exchange" AND actor.key_id: "<key-id>" | sort by timestamp desc | limit 200
- SQL-ish (internal analytics):
  SELECT timestamp, actor_id, action, resource, success, ip FROM audit_events WHERE actor_key = '<key-id>' ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 500;
- Common fields to capture: timestamp, actor_id, actor_key_id, action, resource, request_id, request_body_hash, ip, user_agent, trace_id.

SIEM export checklist (for evidence handoff):
- Time window chosen (UTC): note start and end.
- All query strings used and saved as saved-search in SIEM.
- Export formats: JSON (preferred), PCAP for network captures (if performed), raw log bundles.
- Include corresponding AWS/GCP/Azure audit logs, load balancer logs, and firewall logs.
- Hash exports (SHA256) and record hashes in incident ticket.

Evidence automation hooks (notes for responders):
- Use evidence-collector service: /tools/evidence-collector collect --incident <id> --source audit,app,network --since <ts> --until <ts>
- If automation fails, manually export using SIEM UI and upload to secured incident bucket s3://redwood-ir/secure/<incident-id>/raw/
- Mark evidence retention policy: attach retention tag "ir-temp" which keeps data for 90 days pending legal hold.

Short templates for incident channel messages:
- Initial page (use in #sec-incident-<id>):
  TITLE: [SEV1] Suspected credential compromise — <service>
  SUMMARY: brief 1–2 sentences
  ACTIONS TAKEN: rotated key <id>, revoked sessions for <principal>, isolated host i-01234
  NEXT: SRE applying firewall update; security investigating audit logs
- Major update: "Update — confirmed unauthorized access to service X. Containment in progress. For timeline and artifacts see JIRA-SEC-<id>."
- Resolution: short summary + note to start postmortem.

Postmortem template (copy into Confluence post-incident doc):
- Title: Security postmortem — <short incident title> — JIRA-SEC-<id>
- Author(s): list of names
- Incident timeline: bulletized timeline (UTC) with timestamps and source of each entry (audit id / log file / Slack message link)
- Summary of impact: what data/services/customers affected, approximate duration, severity classification
- Root cause analysis: succinct cause + 5-whys chain (use numbered list)
- Detection: how and when was incident first detected (alert name or manual discovery)
- Containment & remediation steps: what was done and when (include RBAC changes and key rotations)
- Evidence collected: list of artifacts + hash values + s3 path or SIEM export id
- Post-incident actions (owner, ETA): e.g., "automate rotation for key type X — owner: infra-secrets — ETA: 2025-02-15"
- Metrics/telemetry to add: recommended dashboards and queries to detect recurrence
- Lessons learned / process changes: short bullets
- Communication log: links to messages sent to customers/internal execs with timestamps

Artifact checklist (required for a complete postmortem):
- Audit export (JSON) with saved search id
- System logs (ids and hashes)
- Evidence collector bundle id (if used)
- Network pcap (if performed) + filter used
- RBAC change history snapshot (rbacctl diff output)
- Key rotation records + new key fingerprint(s)
- SIEM alerts & saved searches used for detection

Retention & SIEM mapping notes:
- All incident exports should include the audit schema mapping reference (see security-triage-audit-schema-cheatsheet) — ensure fields above are present.
- Mapping key: internal field names -> SIEM fields -> external vendor names (capture in postmortem table).
- Evidence retention: default 90 days for IR temporary holdings; escalate to legal hold for PII/business-critical incidents.

Open questions / unresolved items (working doc style):
- Should token revocation be immediate for all suspected keys or only for high-severity incidents? Pros/cons listed.
- Automating RBAC rollback for false positives — need safe rollback design (owner: platform-engineering).
- Cross-team drill plan: schedule tabletop for RBAC v2 misuse scenario (owner: security-eng).

Quick references & links:
- Full IR runbook (Confluence): CONFLUENCE-IR/SECMGMT-122
- RBAC v2 design doc (Confluence): CONFLUENCE-RBAC/V2-ARCH
- Evidence automation repo: github.com/redwood-inference/tools/evidence-collector
- Escalation contact list (on-call): /internal/oncall/contacts (linked in Jira ticket)

Notes to responders: keep updates short, time-stamped, and factual. Preserve chain of custody by always exporting audit logs from the server-side SIEM and hashing artifacts. For high-severity incidents, involve Legal and Customer Success early.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-07 created by Aisha Kapoor (initial sketch)
- 2024-12-02 updated: added SIEM export checklist (Priya Desai)
- 2025-01-18 updated: added RBAC quick commands and artifact checklist (Ethan Morales)

-- end of quick reference --
